## 1.

ISLP Section 6.2.2 considers a special case with one observation per
coefficient, a design matrix equal to the identity, and no intercept. With
a single coefficient, ridge regression minimizes $(y - \beta)^2 + \lambda\beta^2$
and the lasso minimizes $(y - \beta)^2 + \lambda|\beta|$. The solutions are

$$\hat\beta^R = \frac{y}{1 + \lambda}, \qquad
\hat\beta^L = \begin{cases}
y - \lambda/2 & \text{if } y > \lambda/2, \\
y + \lambda/2 & \text{if } y < -\lambda/2, \\
0 & \text{if } |y| \leq \lambda/2.
\end{cases}$$

a. Take $y = 3$ and $\lambda = 2$. Fill in the code below to plot the ridge criterion against $\beta$ over `np.linspace(-1, 4, 501)` and confirm that it is smallest at $\hat\beta^R$.

::: {.no-answer}
:::

```{python}
y = 3
lam = 2
beta = np.linspace(-1, 4, 501)

# the ridge criterion at each value of beta
ridge_criterion = (y - beta) ** 2 + ____

plt.plot(beta, ridge_criterion)
plt.xlabel("beta")
plt.ylabel("ridge criterion")
plt.show()

# the value of beta where the criterion is smallest
beta_min = beta[np.argmin(ridge_criterion)]
print("smallest on the grid at:", beta_min)
print("formula gives:", ____)
```
